**[p. 186]** Surah "As-Saffat" (The Ranks)

Its main purpose is to establish the proof for the end of Surah Ya-Sin, through the Exalted being free of all deficiencies. What necessarily follows from this is the return of the servants for a judgment between them with justice. What necessarily follows from this is the Oneness (of God). That is the meaning indicated by its name, "As-Saffat," in His words: ﴿And indeed We are those who stand in ranks, and indeed We are those who glorify (Him)﴾ [37:165-166].

"In the name of Allah": that is, the One who possesses absolute perfection, so that no deficiency approaches His presence. "The Most Merciful": the One who bestowed favor through the mercy of justice in both abodes. "The Most Compassionate": the One who bestows favor upon whoever desires obedience through reward and return (to Him), and through removing punishment.

Since sole dominion over the kingdom (malakut) is only possible together with the Oneness of His essence, and in this is the entitlement to exclusive divinity, and since this (although it is such that it is not hidden from anyone of understanding) is, for them, in the utmost remoteness, and for this reason they do not accept what relates to the kingdom and deny it in the utmost denial, it was fitting that He swear an oath concerning it.

And since it is part of eloquence that the oath and what is sworn about be suitably matched, and since lining up in rows indicates unity of purpose, as in the rows of battle and of prayer, and since the angels have no purpose except God, with nothing hindering them from that, they were the most worthy of creation of lining up, at one time for prayer and at another for glorifying and sanctifying, and at another (p. 187) for managing provisions, and at another for punishing the people of discord, and other matters that hearts cannot contain. And they were, after the cry (zajra, a loud shout) of death, then the cry of life, both mentioned in the preceding surah, then the two cries of swooning and reviving, which come in Az-Zumar, at the time when the sky is split open with clouds, and becomes red like oil, and is shattered by the might of the Sovereign, the Judge, and what is in it of bodies and meanings is brought low. The angels of each heaven descend and form a circular row: the angels of the first heaven around the people of the earth, and the angels of the second heaven around the angels of the first, and so on. Then, when it is said: ﴿O assembly of jinn and humankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass through﴾ [55:33], they become (a crowd), and the servants surge against one another from the intensity of the crush and the length of the standing. Whenever they incline in any direction, they (the angels) drive them back with a shout by which they turn them away from passing through. Yet the orderly arrangement of those that govern (affairs), arising from their lining up in governance in obedience to the Mighty King, indicates the Oneness (of God). He (the Exalted) said: ﴿By those who stand in ranks﴾; that is, the companies of angels, and those who pray, and those who strive, perfecting themselves through lining up in obedience. So it is a description of a omitted noun that is feminine in form. He turned away from saying "as-saffin" (those who stand in ranks), which is restricted to male rational beings, so that it would include (p. 188) the companies of angels, jinn, humankind, birds, wild beasts, and others. This is an indication that nothing among them is brought together so that its purpose is unified except by one Almighty; and that no purpose of any of them unifies except that it becomes equal in description, and nothing becomes equal in description except that its shout (zajr) is unified, and its shout is not unified except that what reminds it by its voice is unified; and nothing of that is unified in it except that its purpose succeeds and its right guidance becomes clear. The evidence of direct observation is the clearest of this: when the purpose of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, was unified in raising the religion, while they were the weakest of nations and the fewest in number, no group of people who had no comparison to them in strength or multitude stood against them. Their ranks did not diminish, and their shout wounded and destroyed hearts, and their remembrance expanded and illuminated breasts, as the Exalted indicated at the end of this surah, in His words: ﴿And indeed Our army, they are the victorious﴾ [37:173]. Likewise with non-human beings among the animals, as is seen with mice and locusts: when Allah (the Exalted) wills the unity of their purpose in something, they overcome whoever contends with them, and subdue whoever opposes them or turns them back. Thus it became clear that all good is what is intended by the oath, and it is truly unified with what is sworn about, and it joins and fastens to it with the closest bond, and the meaning of both is perfectly harmonized.

And since emphasis with the verbal noun (masdar) indicates more strongly the intended unity, He said: ﴿ṣaffan﴾ (in rows), which is the arrangement of a group along a line. And since the unity of purpose necessitates the strength that prepares for the shout, and the perfecting of others is caused by and follows from the perfecting of the self, and is more noble than it if it were stripped of perfecting (oneself); and since the perfecting (of others) is only completed and its effect is only greatly magnified together with awe, (the Prophet said): "He seized me, and pressed me down, until the effort reached me" (hadith).

He said, linking with "fa" (so then): ﴿By those who drive away with a driving﴾; that is, those who rebuke, immediately after the line-up, everyone who departs from the command of Allah; ﴿with a driving﴾; that is, rebuking with admonitions and other means, perfecting others.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 37, verse 3:

Since the outpouring (al-ifadah) is caused by good receptiveness (husn al-talaqqi), which is caused by emptying the mind (tafrigh al-bal), which is caused by awe of the one who conveys benefit, and since the outpouring of recitation is the greatest outpouring, He said: ﴿By those who recite﴾; that is, those who follow in reasoning (istidlal) for their own statement and action, and as a preparation for their excuse, and as an honouring of their rank, and as a completion for others: ﴿a reminder﴾; that is, an admonition, and an honouring, and a reminding, from the remembrance of their Lord, an outpouring upon others of the spirit of knowledge. The assimilation of the taa' into the saad, the zay and the dhal (idgham) is an indication that this, despite its terror and magnitude, may remain hidden from anyone other than the one whom God wills to inform of it. For the Cry (al-sayha) shattered the hearts of the unbelievers, from Thamud and others, but did not affect those among them who believed. And Jibril, peace be upon him, used to bring down to the Prophet ﷺ what he brought of the Qur'an, while the Companions, may God be pleased with them, were around him, not hearing any of it. And God is the Granter of success.

﴿Indeed your God﴾, that is, the One you have taken as gods besides Him, ﴿is One﴾. That is, dividing (the divinity) brings no good, because of the deep incapacity that accompanies it, which is far from perfection. Divinity cannot exist at all without the One who has none of that incapacity. ﴿To Him alone﴾, not to anyone else, ﴿you will be returned, so that He may judge between you concerning that about which you differed.﴾ He is the One who sent down this Book in His might and mercy, and protected it from confusion and other things, as He will mention through His greatness and majesty. Had He not been One, the order of this lining-up, of the admonition, of the recitation, and of what follows from them would have been disrupted, and the order of this existence, which we witness, would have been disrupted too. We witness this in the affairs of kingdoms when kings differ, in the changing of customs and the abrogation (naskh, the cancelling of an earlier ruling by a later one) of laws that earlier ones had firmly established, along with all the effects and properties that belong to them. Yet we witness this existence as He, glory be to Him and exalted, has firmly ordained it, with nothing in it changing from the state He has set for it. So He has taught us that He is necessarily One, uniquely singular in greatness, with no equal to Him, beyond any doubt.

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: When Surat Ya-Sin contained great admonition and profound guidance, through which the one granted success is guided by considering some of it, and through which the one who reflects occupies himself in attaining its aim and obligation, and which testifies that the Sovereign in its entirety is One, even if the nose of the stubborn and the denier is rubbed in the dust, He (exalted) followed it with an oath concerning His oneness. He (exalted) said: ﴿By those who line up in rows﴾ [al-Saffat: 1], and so on, up to His saying (exalted): ﴿Indeed your God is One﴾, up to His saying: ﴿Lord of the easts﴾ [al-Saffat: 5]. Then the discourse returned to admonition concerning His wondrous creations, and He (exalted) said: ﴿Indeed We have adorned the lowest heaven with the adornment of the stars﴾ [al-Saffat: 6], up to His saying: ﴿a piercing flame﴾ [al-Saffat: 10]. Then He followed with mention of the obstinacy of the one who denies, along with clarification of the matter and its clarity, and the weakness of what they were created from: ﴿Indeed We created them from sticky clay﴾ [al-Saffat: 11].

Then he mentioned their deeming the otherworldly return improbable, the great bewilderment that would seize them, and their regret when they witness what they had denied. The verses then joined to the mention of the messengers along with their peoples, and their course of obstinacy, hesitation and denial, following closely similar patterns, and the taking of each for his sin, and the deliverance of the messengers of God and his party, and the perpetuation of the good remembrance of them through their being chosen and drawn near. Then the discourse returned to rebuking the polytheists and clarifying the falsehood of the transgressors, up to the end of the surah. End.

Since His oneness was established, it produced His description with His saying: ﴿Lord﴾; that is, the Originator, the Owner, the King, and the Manager of ﴿the heavens﴾; that is, the lofty bodies; ﴿and the earth﴾; that is, the lowly bodies; ﴿and what is between them﴾; that is, of the filled expanse, with its companions and helpers, in such number that the powers cannot count it. And this, although it is the result of what preceded, is suitable to be an evidence for it, because of what it indicates of the orderly arrangement of management, which cannot be realized with plurality. Just as the oath sworn by here is also an indication of the evidence of oneness, in that it is in one order always in obedience, which was indicated by the ranks, the restraining, and the recitation. So glory be to the One who made this Qur'an miraculous in its order, wondrous in its matter, and far-reaching in its aim.

Since the context concerns bounty through recitation and other things, and the direction of sunrise is the direction of bounty through the manifest self-disclosure that brings the hidden into being, which necessitates transcendence above deficiencies, and since the whole was more fitting for the choosing that regards the subjugation alongside harmony, He said: ﴿And Lord of the easts﴾; that is, the three hundred and sixty, in which the sun, the moon, and all the wandering stars manifest themselves to you each day, over the passing of ages, years, months, and days, in an order that does not loosen and a course that does not change or go awry. Mention of them necessarily indicates the wests, because they differ by them. He repeated the description with them, to draw attention to the clarity of its indication, with what it contains of that for which the context is meant, of lining up, which indicates the goodness of harmony, and to indicate resurrection through the signs after disappearance.

When the places of rising (al-mashariq) call for outpouring and manifestation, He followed that with its outcome: that which by its nature rises and sets, even if only through concealment and appearance. So He said, emphasizing it and turning the speech to the first person plural of majesty, as an alert that their conduct is the conduct of one who denies the stars' adornment and what they indicate of His greatness, glory be to Him, and He magnified the expression of the adornment by doubling the verb for such a matter: ﴿Indeed We have adorned﴾, that is, by Our majesty which cannot be approached, ﴿the heaven﴾. Since they could only see the heavens nearest to them, and the adornment of the stars was manifest in them, He said ﴿the nearest﴾, that is, the heaven which is nearest to you.

When it was indicated that the arrangement is an adornment inwardly, through the unity of purpose, just as it is an adornment outwardly through beauty of form and wondrous ordering, the alert to this was increased by repeating what was understood from "We adorned" in His saying ﴿with an adornment of the stars﴾, that is, with the adornment belonging to the bright, luminous, sparkling, fixed stars in their places, whether stationary or moving, set into the sky like the studs of inlay, shining like the flowers of light scattered over the bright green of gardens. So it is, with the absence of tanwin and of the genitive case, an explicative genitive construction (idafa bayaniyya, a construction in which the second noun specifies the first), like "a garment of silk." As for one who reads "the adornment" with tanwin: if he puts "the stars" in the genitive, it is in apposition (badal), that is, "with the stars which are an adornment." If he puts it in the accusative, it is for praise, with the implied "I mean." Or it is a substitution of inclusion (badal ishtimal, where the substitute is part of or connected to what it replaces) from "the heaven," that is, its stars, either because they are in the air below it, so one supposes they are in it, or because they are in it from the side that faces us, or because it is transparent through them, even though some of them are above it. Its adornment is their orderly arrangement and their configuration in this wondrous pattern, in varied forms and marvelous shapes, between small and large, some of them fixed, some wandering, some rising, (p-195) some setting, and other states beyond these which cannot be counted and have no limit known to the weak servants, so that they could be fully enumerated.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 37, verse 7:

Since the existence of one thing for many things is more indicative of power and more manifest in majesty, he said, indicating by conjunction (ʿaṭf) with something that has no apparent preceding conjunct, with an implied element (muqaddar) that shows that adorning the heaven with stars is an intended matter and not a coincidental one: ﴿And as a guard﴾; that is, We adorned it with them for ornamentation, and for guarding ﴿from every rebellious devil﴾; that is, one distant from good, burning. And since the intention is generalization in guarding from every transgressor, whether he is extreme in rebellion or not, he said: ﴿defiant﴾; that is, stripped of good, transgressing in every evil, whether he reaches the furthest extremes of that or is at the lowest degrees of it, like "ḍārib" (one who strikes) and "ḍarrāb" (one who strikes much).

Since the aim in the two surahs, an-Nisa and al-Hajj, was to censure the disbelievers for doing what is not in its nature evil, and for debasing themselves by following what there is no doubt is base, by their distance from good after having concealed it, He expressed it with *al-marid* (the rebellious one), for emphasis. Just as He guarded the visible sky with what He mentioned, glorified and exalted is He, so too He adorned the hearts of the saints, which are like the sky for the lands of their bodies, with the stars of gnosis. When a phantom (*tayf*) from Satan touches them, they remember, and the meteors of their states, their gnosis, and their words pelt it. When the listener became eager to know this protection, its fruit, and an explanation of its manner, He resumed with His saying: ﴿They cannot listen﴾, meaning: the devils implied by "every devil" will never have any hearing at all.

Ibn al-Jawzi said: al-Farra' said: "*la* (not) here is like His saying: ﴿Thus We have inserted it into the hearts of the criminals; they will not believe in it﴾. In this sense, *la* may carry the meaning of a jussive (*jazm*). The Arabs say: 'I tied it to something that will not slip loose.'" End of quote.

The universal quantifier "every" and then the plural, considering the meaning, and the singular for the pronoun of "the snatcher" and for "the snatching," indicate that they are removed from hearing, both the collective and its individual members, and that snatching occurs, if it happens, to one individual and not to a group, and from one individual and not a group, and only for a word or what is similar to it, and no more. The sound hadith points to this: "That word is from the truth, which the jinn snatches away." He emphasized their distance by affirming the particle of limit (*ghayah*), and so said, with *sami'a* (to hear) implicit in its meaning after restricting it to the sense of "to end" (*intaha*), or "to give ear" (*asgha*), so that the meaning becomes: their hearing, their eavesdropping, or their listening does not reach: ﴿to the High Assembly﴾, meaning: the great and noble gathering. The reading of the one who doubled the *sin* and the *mim* clarifies this meaning (p-197), in the sense of "they eavesdrop" (*yatasamma'una*), meaning by some kind of trick, an eavesdropping that reaches up to that point. It implies that they do eavesdrop, but their eavesdropping does not reach what was mentioned, as the doubling indicates. It also indicates that they strive hard to conceal their affair. He used the singular adjective also to indicate that the seizing occurs from one individual and not a group, so He said: ﴿the Highest﴾, meaning: in place and in rank, such that they fill the eyes with splendor and the hearts with awe.

Since the implied meaning is "because they are driven away with a strong expulsion," He indicated this by the conjunction in His saying: ﴿and they are pelted﴾, meaning: the devils are struck with a violent, rapid striking by which they are driven away. It is in the passive voice because what matters is their being pelted, not identifying the one who pelts them, although it is more indicative of the Divine power, exalted is He and glorified: ﴿from every side﴾, meaning: from all directions of the heavens, with the meteors, when they seek to hear by stealing.

﴿Repulsion﴾; that is, a casting that repels them, driving them away, humbled and banished. It is then an emphasis (ta'kid) on the casting by meaning, or an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu, the object showing the reason for an action), or a circumstantial state (hal, an accusative describing the condition of the subject at the time of the action).

Since this might lead someone to suppose that they are not subject to Divine power in any state other than this one, or by any means other than this kind, He informed that they are in His grip. He made their condition this a trial for whichever of His servants He wills. So He said, using the lam (the preposition "for," which is commonly used to express benefit), in mockery of them: ﴿And for them is a punishment﴾; that is, in this world, by this and by other means, and in the Hereafter, on the Day of the Great Gathering; ﴿perpetual﴾; that is, lasting, causing illness, painful, greatly causing pain, persistent in that, constant upon it. This is so even though the two durations differ in continuity, magnitude, intensity, and pain. (p-198)

Since the guarding of the Qur'an by the power of the Sovereign, the Judge (al-Dayyan), against the intrusion of the jinn has thus been established; and some of them, despite this, would at times hear what God wished them to hear, so that He might make it a trial for whomever of His servants He wills, together with the Qur'an's distinction by its inimitability—He made an exception from the subject of "yasamma'un" (they eavesdrop), with His saying: ﴿except one who snatches a fragment﴾. He indicated the rarity of this by using the singular pronoun, with His saying: ﴿the snatching﴾; i.e., he stole a word, or more than one word, one time out of the times, from among them. He indicated the strength of the swooping of the stars in his pursuit by the hamza in His saying: ﴿so a flaming meteor pursued him﴾, even though the verb is transitive without it; i.e., it followed him with the utmost speed, as if it were driving itself and following him closely; as if God—glorified is He and exalted is His majesty—had prepared it so that it would never swoop except in the wake of whoever had heard from them at the moment of hearing, equally, without fail. ﴿A flaming meteor﴾: i.e., a flame of fire from a star or something else. ﴿Piercing﴾: i.e., it pierces whatever it strikes, of jinn or others. Even if the jinn is made of fire, it is not pure fire. Granting this, the one thing may be of several kinds, some stronger than others, so the stronger affects the weaker, like iron. Sometimes it misses the jinn, and sometimes it hits him; and when it hits him, sometimes it burns him, destroying him, and sometimes it merely weakens him.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 37, verse 11:

Since the main purpose of this Greatest Book (al-Kitab al-A'zam) is to explain the four foundational principles: tawhid (the oneness of God); prophethood (nubuwwah); the return (al-ma'ad, the resurrection and the Hereafter); and the affirmation of qada' and qadar (divine decree and predestination); and since He, glory be to Him, indicated through these matters He has mentioned His existence, the perfection of His knowledge, the completeness of His power over awe-inspiring acts, and the wondrous nature of His wisdom, from which the affirmation of His oneness necessarily follows, as a detailed explanation of part of the general statement: ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth...?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 81], then what lies below them of acts is more fitting (for Him to create); He, on the basis of this, for the sake of establishing the gathering (al-hashr) which this Qur'an has reported, the Qur'an which He guarded against the deceptions of the jinn by the adornment of the stars, from which He made the piercing meteors, said, mocking them: ﴿So ask them﴾; that is: ask them to give a verdict (yatafattawu, from fatwa) by explaining to you what you ask them about, regarding their denial of the resurrection. Its root is from "futuwwah," which is generosity. ﴿Are they more difficult﴾; that is: stronger, harder, and more arduous ﴿in creation﴾; that is: in terms of the perfection of craftsmanship, its strength, and its magnitude. ﴿Or those whom﴾; since the intent is to inform that there is nothing among the existent things except that it is His creation, glory be to Him, He expressed it with what indicates that, without mentioning "We," so that it would be more general; and He omitted the object because it is understood, and so that it would not cause confusion when the pronoun of those being asked is mentioned. Then He said: ﴿We created﴾; that is: from these things We have enumerated, from the living and others, from the jinn whom We gave the capacity to reach the celestial sphere, and others; and He expressed it with "whom" (man), giving precedence to the rational beings among the angels and others, among what lies between the heavens and the earth.

Since the answer is certainly that these created things are stronger in creation than they are, and that they are among the weakest of creatures in creation, He said, indicating by it the intent of mocking them in the question, emphasizing (it), pointing out that their denial of resurrection, because they deem it unlikely to distinguish dust from dust, necessarily entails denial of the origination of creation in this manner: ﴿Indeed, We created them﴾; that is: in accordance with Our greatness; ﴿from clay﴾; that is: from loose, base dust; ﴿sticky﴾ (lazib); that is: intensely mixed, one part with another, so that it adhered, compacted, became constricted, and one part clung to another, became scarce yet strong, some of its parts entered into others, hardened and became firm, so that distinguishing one part of it from another became more difficult than distinguishing some dust scattered from other dust. Ibn al-Jawzi said: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "It is pure, good, sticky clay."

They were from clay because their father Adam was created from it, without a father or mother; so by this estimation they became part of the clay, which is part of His creation that He enumerated before that, glory be to Him and exalted. It is known that the state of clay is far removed from their state; but they were (created) by His power, glory be to Him, His essential power, which nothing can resist, and which no command can overwhelm. Thus the origination of their creation, and the creation of what is stronger and greater than them, indicates with certainty the power to restore them, and indeed by way of greater priority in many respects. This questioning was made most fitting by concluding the preceding discourse with those who rose to the heavens in arrogance and haughtiness, and who aspired to what they could not attain, in tyranny and haughtiness; and He set upon them what would turn them back, subdued, distanced, and rejected; and He excepted from them the one who "snatched" (the stolen word), so that it would be known that what their hopes clung to is not impossible. This is along with His mention of their creation from sticky clay, whose nature is to sink because of its weight and to descend, just as the nature of those with whom He concluded what came before is to rise and ascend because of their lightness.

Since it is certainly known that the purpose of this command to seek a ruling (*istifta'*) is only rebuke (*tabkit*, censure), because it is certainly known that the answer is: "They are not stronger in creation than that, so their resurrection is not impossible. Nor is their overcoming the Messenger of the One, the Subduer, whom He has made judge in this Revelation by making him prevail over all religion, possible in any way, either by transmission or by reason. So they have no doubt in denying it, nor in their assumption that they will overcome Our Messenger. Rather, they are in a state of great wonder at their denial of it and at their assumption that they will prevail in this world." He expressed this by His saying, attributing the wonder to the most exalted of the existent or the most exalted of the created beings, glorifying it, meaning that it is a statement that deserves to be said about it: that one does not know what caused it or what was the reason for committing it. So He said: ﴿Rather, you wonder﴾ (p-202), with a *ḍamma* on the *tā'*, according to the reading of Ḥamzah and al-Kisā'ī, drawing attention to the statement from the position of majesty, to explicitly attribute the wonder to Him, glorified is He, as an indication that this wonder has reached a limit that cannot be described, since it is attributed to One who is exempt from it. With a *fatḥa* on it, according to the rest of the readers, meaning: at their audacity in denying the resurrection. Especially since the Qur'an has pointed to it in these strange expressions and wondrous, marvellous aspects, which no one with even minimal understanding doubts. The Prophet (ﷺ) had assumed, as is fitting, that no one would hear the Qur'an without believing in it. Al-Qushayrī said: The reality of wonder is a change in the soul by something whose cause is hidden, of a kind for which the custom has not been to occur the like of it. Similar to this is the hadith of the two Ṣaḥīḥs (*al-Ṣaḥīḥayn*), from Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Umm Sulaym and Abū Ṭalḥah (may Allah be pleased with them both): "Allah laughed, and in another narration: wondered, at your deeds tonight." And the hadith of al-Bukhārī (may Allah have mercy on him), also from Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him): "Our Lord wonders at people who are led into Paradise in chains." Similar to these there are many, and the meaning in all of them is to draw attention to the greatness of the act and that it is extraordinary, contrary to custom. It is also possible that the meaning is that they did not deny it because of the scarcity of evidence for it; rather, there has come from its evidences what causes a great wonder because of its abundance and the long patience in its successive repetition. ﴿And they mock﴾, meaning: the wonder has arisen in you, while they keep renewing their mockery whenever you bring them a proof.

And when they are reminded, they do not remember. That is: when they are admonished by any admonisher, with something they know very well, which points them to the Resurrection, like what they are reminded of concerning power, even though it is not permissible in the intellect of any intelligent person among them that anyone would leave those under his hand without accountability. "They do not remember" means: they do not act in accordance with what the reminder requires.

When He mentioned their turning away from what is heard, He followed it with their turning away from what is seen, saying: ﴿And when they see a sign﴾; that is, a sign (ʿalāma) of the truthfulness of the Messenger (ﷺ) and of others; ﴿they mock it﴾; that is, they seek to make it an object of mockery (al-sukhriyya) by it, with some of them calling one another to that, out of the intensity of their ridicule.

Since their denial of the Resurrection, even if it occurred only once, was so monstrous, grave and vile—like their renewing their mockery every time they heard a verse, and exaggerating in it—and since its proofs are so manifest and clear, being far from doubts, He expressed this with the past tense, saying: ﴿And they said﴾; that is, what is utterly strange: ﴿"This is not"﴾; that is, what: ﴿"this"﴾; that is, what He brought to us concerning the matter of the Resurrection and other things which we have witnessed or which he informed us of: ﴿"except sorcery"﴾; that is, illusion and deceptive matters that have no realities: ﴿"clear"﴾; that is, manifest in itself, and making its mockery apparent.

Then they singled out the resurrection for denial: "When we have died, will we really...?" (﴿أإذا مِتْنا﴾). They then joined to it what, in their view, makes denial even stronger, saying: "and we have become" (﴿وكُنّا﴾), meaning a state of having become thoroughly established: "dust" (﴿تُرابًا﴾). They placed dust first because it points more clearly to their intended meaning, since it is furthest from life. "And bones" (﴿وعِظامًا﴾). It is as if they made each of death and becoming (al-kawn) an obstacle to resurrection, whether it be pure dust, pure bone, or a mixture of the two. This is despite their acknowledgment that the beginning of their creation was from dust, a point that is very clear. "But minds that their Creator has led astray" (a saying: "but there are minds which their Maker has led astray"). Then they repeated the interrogative of denial, according to the reading of those who recited it that way, for added emphasis, saying: ﴿أإنّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ﴾ ("Will we indeed be raised up?").

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 37, verse 17:

When the meaning was: "Will our resurrection be established?", they joined to it their statement, repeating the interrogative of denial (al-istifham al-inkari) for emphasis of the increase in their far-fetching (istib'ad) of it, to the point that they were certain it was impossible; so they said a feeble statement: ﴿And our forefathers, the earlier ones?﴾ That is: will our resurrection be established, and likewise our forefathers? They increased the far-fetching with their saying ﴿the earlier ones﴾, that is, those whose stay in the earth under layers of soil had been long, whose parts had been reduced to dust, such that no trace of them remained at all, the ages had passed, and not one of them had been raised up on any day of the days, so that his resurrection would show us the truth of what is claimed about that.

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 37, verse 18:

When they had gone to such extremes in denying it, after the proofs had been established in this surah and elsewhere for its possibility, indeed its customary necessity, He commanded him to answer them with what corresponds to that. So He (Exalted is He) said: ﴿Say: Yes﴾; meaning, you will be resurrected under every supposition you have posited. He described their state with His words: ﴿and you will be humbled﴾; meaning, compelled to it, abased, humiliated, belittled.

Then he gave a reason, based on the certainty of its occurrence, that shows it is an extreme degradation, so he said: ﴿Then it will be only﴾; that is, it will happen because you will be driven, so you will rise. The driving [zajra] by which they rise is ﴿but a single cry﴾; that is, a shout (ṣayḥa). He emphasised what the word "single" implies, to make clear their denial, and to belittle the matter of resurrection compared with His power, glory be to Him, so He said: ﴿single﴾, which is the second [blast], by which the death of all living beings occurred at once, in one instant, with a similar [cry]. The root meaning of zajr (driving, rebuking) is scolding, and it is used for urging or for prohibiting. This happens only to one who is capable and who has done what angers the one who drives; for this reason the shout was called a zajra.

Since this statement implies anger, he confirmed it by turning the speech away from addressing them, placing them in a position of distance, and generalising it to others. So he said, expressing it with the causal and immediate fa' (fa') and the particle of surprise: ﴿and behold, they﴾; that is, all the dead, in their inner selves and outward forms, the earlier and the later among them, ﴿are [alive], looking﴾; that is, immediately, without any delay at all. There is no difference between one who has entirely become dust, one who has not changed at all, and one who is in between. Perhaps he singled out sight for mention because it does not occur except with full life; for this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When the soul is taken, the sight follows it." As for hearing, it may occur in one who is not alive, because the Prophet (ﷺ) said about the unbelievers among the dead of Badr: "You are no more able to hear what I say than they are." I myself witnessed, in the land of al-ʿUqrūb, near Banyas, in the lands of Syria, a thorn bush called "al-Ghubayrāʾ"; whenever it was said beside it, "Bring me the sickle so I can cut this bush," its leaves began to wilt at once. God knows best the cause of that.

"And when the purpose of depicting their state through this present-tense verb had been achieved, He joined to it [a verb] in the past form (ṣīgat al-maḍī), whose meaning is the future, to inform [us] of the certainty of the matter, [its] certainty being like that of what has passed and occurred, and its certainty being equal to its happening, without any delay and without any interval of time at all. So He said: ﴿And they will say﴾; that is, every disbeliever whom the Resurrection has gathered, informing [one another] of what has been revealed to them: that there is no companion for them other than woe. ﴿Woe to us!﴾; that is, O You whom we have no boon-companion other than Him. ﴿This is the Day of Judgment﴾; that is, of recompense, for every doer [of deeds]."

Since their saying this is only an expression of regret over what they missed of the beneficial belief in it, they added to it by saying, while addressing one another, as an apposition (*badal*) or a description following a description, indicating by the repetition of the demonstrative (*ism al-ishara*, demonstrative pronoun) the terror that had overcome them: ﴿This is the Day of Judgment﴾; i.e., the day on which judgment is passed between the adversaries. Then they added more anguish, grief and lamentation by saying, turning from speaking about it to addressing it directly, because that is more indicative of blaming one another and further from fairness in acknowledgment: ﴿the one you used to deny﴾; i.e., O callers to ruin, by innate disposition and nature. They placed the prepositional phrase (*al-jar*, "bihi," "by it") first, indicating the magnitude of their denial of it. While they were in this state of regret, the call suddenly emerged with what calms their strength and settles their hearts, and both of them are for those who do not disobey God in what He commands and do what they are commanded, from the angels, stern and harsh, to humiliate them and degrade them. To show the speed of that, without any pause, he dropped whatever indicates the call, such as his saying: "It was said to the angels," or "We said," or "The call emerged from the side of Our authority," or the like.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 37, verse 22:

﴿Gather⦆i.e., assemble them with compulsion, humiliation and abasement, O you who are entrusted with the servants from among the angels (ajnad, "troops"). He made their description, which necessitates their doom, more explicit, saying: ﴿those who did wrong﴾, i.e., by what they were engaged in during the world, by placing things in other than their proper places, through the confusion which none commits except one who is in the deepest darkness. ﴿And their spouses﴾, i.e., their followers who followed their example in that kind of wrongdoing, and their counterparts in it from among the jinn and others, and whoever helped them, even with half a word, or was pleased with their deed, so that each group is set apart; some of them will rebuke others, and some of them will revile others. ﴿And what they used to worship﴾, i.e., by what their crooked natures called them to; ﴿worship﴾, i.e., persevering in worshipping it in hope of its benefit, confirming their loss through the certainty of their reliance on what is not a reliable support. It encompasses that which is truly worshipped, or metaphorically through adornment. ﴿Except those for whom the best [reward] has preceded﴾ is an exception by the verse of al-Anbiya' (al-Anbiya', 21:101).

Al-Biqa'i indicated the low rank of their objects of worship, and the foolishness of their opinions in adopting harm (to themselves), by His saying, turning the style away from the first person, even though the majesty would have allowed it, to something greater than it: ﴿besides Allah﴾; that is, the One who is singular in the attributes of majesty and the qualities of perfection. What is meant is those who were content with their being worshipped and did not denounce that from them, nor command them to the Oneness of Allah.

Since they had followed in the world the path of spiritual misery, they deserved to be bound on the Day of Resurrection to follow its sensory path. Therefore, the command to gather them is followed by His saying, in mockery of them and as a cause of their regret: ﴿So guide them﴾; that is, direct them with a guidance that leaves them no doubt, so that they may know, along with the compulsion they are under to follow it, their final destination, and that this will be greater in their distress. Al-Razi said: The root of guidance (hidayah) is going ahead, and the Arabs call the one who goes first "hadi" (guide); it is said, "the forelegs of the horses came forward" (hawadi al-khayl), that is, their necks; and "al-hadiyah" is the staff, because it goes ahead of the one who holds it; and "so-and-so looked at the direction (hadi) of his affair", that is, its direction.

Then He indicated the length of their standing and the evil of their station, by His saying, with the particle of termination: ﴿to the path of the Blazing Fire﴾; that is, the way of the Fire, intensely blazing and clearly visible, about which there is no confusion among them that it will drive them and lead them into it. He singled out this name to inform of its intense blazing, its great flaring, the depth of its bottom, the vastness of its engulfing—through some of it piling upon others—the strength of its kindling, the loftiness of its status, its consuming, the harshness of its agitation, its burning, its enveloping of those within it, and its constriction. In it there is also mockery of them, in that they are in a condition other than what they were in the world of mutual support and solidarity.

Since the purpose of informing them of the path to Hellfire first was to increase their regret, he stated explicitly what the particle of limit (ḥarf al-ghāya) conveys of prolonged detention, so he said: ﴿Stop them﴾; that is, detain them standing, after frightening them with that guidance which error had caused, so that its fruit was wretchedness. Their being halted is at the Path (al-ṣirāṭ); al-Baghawi transmitted this from the exegetes, and said: because questioning takes place at the Path. Then he gave the reason for that with his words: ﴿Indeed, they are to be questioned﴾. By this word he gathered upon them anxieties, so that their imaginings would go every which way, and no regret would remain without being present before them, and no calamity without settling upon their hearts and overpowering them. For the accountable person is entirely weakness and vulnerability, so the place of questioning is for him the greatest regret.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 37, verse 25:

When they were made to stand in this humiliating station, the distress that had befallen them occupied them from the "qāla" (said) and the "qīla" (it was said). They were called out from the station of might and the veil of majesty and dominance, as an increase in their regret, their rebuke, and their reproach, and as a turning away from the context of the third person to direct address, indicating the greatest disappointment: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?﴾ That is: what has happened to you that has occupied and distracted you, while ﴿you do not help one another﴾, that is, one of you does not help another, and they compete in that as rivals compete, the people of resolve, firmness, pride and zeal, even with the slightest help, by what the dropping of the taa' implies; or after delay and devising a stratagem, as indicated by the reading of al-Bazzi from Ibn Kathir, with the madd (elongation) and idgham (assimilation): "Where is your saying about Badr: 'We are a united company, victorious'?" expressing by what indicates the firmness of mutual support.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 37, verse 26:

When what had befallen them of the matter was such as to bring about their dismay and to dull their perception and sensation, he indicated this by placing them in the position of the third person (ghayba), which signals distance, saying, turning away from what its implied sense would be, "They do not help one another": ﴿Rather, they are today submitting (mustaslimun)﴾. He increased in magnifying that time and in reminding of it, saying: ﴿today submitting﴾; that is, their submission is established for them with a steadfastness that has no end, while some of them have forsaken others, [they are] producing submission (al-Islam), that is, surrender (al-inqiyad), producing it as one who seems to seek it and magnifies in it his desire, hoping that this would lighten that for them.

When He informed that they were questioned and did not answer, it might have been thought that they had been struck dumb. So He drew attention to the fact that they speak in ways that only increase their distress. He said, conjoining it to His words, ﴿And they will say, "Woe to us! This is the Day of Recompense"﴾ [al-Saffat 37:20], indicating their engagement in dispute (khisam) once the standing was complete and they began to move their feet, walking in the manner of a gathered and crowded throng, toward the places of distress and grief. He did not join it with the particle fa' (so/then), because it is not a result caused by the standing nor by the halting for questioning, unlike what comes concerning the people of Paradise. ﴿And some of them turned toward others﴾, that is, those who did wrong, ﴿questioning one another﴾, that is, after their being halted and rebuked. He expressed their dispute mockingly, with His words ﴿questioning﴾, that is, the questioning of adversaries.

When it was as if it had been asked, "About what?", he was answered by His saying: ﴿They will say﴾, that is, the followers to their leaders. By the particle of being (*kāna*) he indicates persistence in their misguiding them, and he emphasizes it, to refute the leaders' denial of it: ﴿Indeed, you used to come to us﴾. Since they were enticing them and inciting them with what their minds accept, in accordance with their customary practices, to the point that they were certain of this, like one who intends to go somewhere, then takes an omen (*tiyara*, augury) from the bird passing on the right (*sanih*) or on the left (*barih*), sees what he likes, and proceeds toward it while certain of its occurrence, they alluded to this by their saying: ﴿you would come to us﴾, passing by us, ﴿from the right﴾, that is, from strength, coercion, dominance, and authority, in your leading us into error. So we acted in your obedience like one who went out for a need, saw what made him proceed toward it. This was the cause of our disbelief.

This practice of augury (*tafa'ul*) was one whose manner the Arabs forgot when the Sharia abrogated it (*nasakha*), as happened with the gambling arrows (*maysir*). Therefore the speech of the lexicographers became confused in explaining it.

The author of al-Qamus said: "*al-Barih* from game animals: what passes from your right side to your left." And "*sanaha al-zabyu sunuhan*" (the gazelle passed from right to left): the opposite of "*barih*." Ibn al-Qattaf said, in the book *al-Af'al*: "*sanaha al-shay'* *sunuhan*": it became easy. And "*al-ta'ir* and *al-zaby*": it passed from your right to your left, and he takes it as a good omen. He also said under the root *barih*: "*Barih al-ta'ir and al-zaby and others*": the opposite of *sanah*, which is what shows you its right side. The people of the Hijaz consider it inauspicious, while others consider it auspicious, and they consider the *sanih* inauspicious.

Ibn Maktum said, in *al-Jam' bayn al-'Ubab wa al-Muhkam*, under the root *barih*: "*al-Barih*" is the opposite of *al-sanih*, and "*qad barihal-zaby*" when it passes you on its left side, moving from your right to your left. The Arabs take omens from the *barih*.

Under the root *sanah*: "*al-sanih*" is what comes to you from your right, of a gazelle, a bird, or other things. "*Al-barih*" is what comes to you from that on your left. It was also said: "*al-sanih*" is what passes you on its right side, and "*al-barih*" is what passes you on its left side. It was also said: "*al-sanih*" is what comes from your right, so that its left side faces your left.

The Arabs differ in the interpretation of this augury. Some of them take an omen of good from the *sanih* and an omen of ill from the *barih*. On this basis is the proverb: "Who can give me the *sanih* after the *barih*?" The author of al-Qamus said: that is, the blessed after the ill-omened.

Others take an omen of ill from the *sanih*. Imam Abu 'Abd Allah al-Qazzaz said, under the root *sanah*: "*al-sanih* from birds, gazelles, and others is the one that comes to you from your right, taking to your left, so that its left side is turned toward you, and it is possible for you to throw at it. Most Arabs take an omen of good from it." He said under the root *barih*: "*al-barih* from birds and gazelles is the opposite of *al-sanih*: it is the one that meets you with its left side turned away from your left. It is one of the things the people of al-'Aliyah take an omen of good from, and they take an omen of ill from the *sanih*. The *sanih* is the one that meets you with its right side turned away from your right. It is one of the things the people of Najd take an omen of good from and take an omen of ill from the *barih*."

The *barih* is clearer in ill omen than the *sanih*, because the *barih* is the one that takes from your left to your right, so you cannot strike it, and so it is considered ill-omened because it is difficult for the one who would spear or shoot it.

For this reason Abu Dawud said:

*I said, when they emerged from a hilltop,*
*"The wild ass has lied, even if it passed on the left."*

He means: it lied when it hoped to escape, even though it had passed on the left and was difficult to strike. Whoever takes an omen of good from it is optimistic about its safety and escape from the spearman. Whoever takes an omen of ill from the *sanih* is pessimistic that it passes from your right to your left so that you can strike it. Whoever takes an omen of ill from it is pessimistic about its lack of safety and its falling into what he hates.

From birds there is also the *jabih*, which meets you face to face. Also the *nатӣh* (striker), and the *qa'id*, which comes to you from behind you. This is what I have found of the speech of the lexicographers on this matter, so understand it.

The apparent meaning, as the verse conveys, is that the Arabs agreed that what came from the right was blessed, whether it came from in front, facing you, and passed toward the back, so that its right side was turned toward you, or came from the right side, whether its beginning of coming was from behind or not, then passed in front of you sideways toward the left, so that its left side was turned toward you in both cases. What came from the left side, in contrast, was ill-omened.

It seems they differed in naming. Most of them named the first *sanih*, from *al-sunh* (with a *damma*), which is good fortune and blessing, from the saying "*sanaha li ra'y*" (an opinion became easy for me), because the meaning of good fortune is well known among them regarding this. The second they named *barih*, from *al-barh*, which is hardship and evil, because this meaning is well known among them under the root *barih*.

Some reversed this, naming the first *barih*, from *al-barhah*, which is a she-camel among the best of camels, because this is well known among them. They named the second *sanih*, from their saying "*sanahahu 'amma arad*" (he turned him away from what he wanted), meaning he diverted him, and "*sanah bi al-rajul wa 'alayhi*": he expelled him, or struck him with evil.

From this difference in naming the disagreement arose. For this reason, Glorified and Exalted is He expressed the meaning and not the name, because His speech does not specify one people over others.

As for the explanation by the possibility of striking and shooting, it has no meaning, because a person turns from his standing position with the slightest movement, so the matter of the left and the right is reversed in relation to him, and the situation of striking and shooting changes. This is if it is granted that striking and shooting are difficult from the left side, which is not granted. And if the meaning revolved around this, the matter would not have been disputed, except in relation to a left-handed person and others, not in relation to the people of al-'Aliyah and others.

As for the verse he cited as evidence, it can be interpreted to mean that its speaker was in need of something he could not do without. He saw the *barih*, so he did not take an omen from it, and he persisted in his matter, denying what the Arabs understood it to indicate.

As for the *jabih* and others, they are other names for certain types of each of the *sanih* and the *barih*. And God knows best.

Abu Hatim Ahmad ibn Hamdan al-Razi said in his book *al-Zinah*: "*al-'iyafah*, *al-qiyafah*, and *al-zajr* are a type of soothsaying (*kahanah*), except that it is lighter in disapproval. That is because the soothsayer was in the position of a judge, and among the soothsayers were some who were worshipped as idols are worshipped, and they were custodians of the idols."

I say: the *kahin* (soothsayer) in the language is the one who judges by the unseen, and that is the utmost of knowledge. So it is a description that indicates deep immersion in knowledge. End of quotation.

Abu Hatim said: I heard some people of literature say: "*al-kahin*" in Hebrew means the knowledgeable one. They called Aaron, peace be upon him, *kahna rabba*, meaning "the knowing one of the Lord."

Then he said: Soothsaying and sorcery were, among the earlier people, a kind of knowledge, so the sorcerer and the soothsayer were both praiseworthy titles. When God brought Islam, these two titles became blameworthy among the Muslims, when He revealed what evil is in them.

Then he said: As for the *'a'if* (augur), *qa'if* (tracker), and *zajir* (one who drives away birds), their path was not like this, meaning like the soothsayer in that they were sometimes worshipped. He said: It was disliked only because it reported something unseen, so it was disliked just as the matter of the stars was disliked, out of caution that it might become like claiming knowledge of the unseen.

The *'a'if* is the one who observes birds, drives them away, and takes lessons from their names, their cries, their landing places, and their flight paths. When he hears the cry of a bird, or it moves from his right to his left, or from his left to his right, he decides by it on good or evil regarding the matter he wants to do. If he decides on evil, that matter is avoided. It is said: "*'afa, ya'ifu*" when he does this. The meaning of "*'afa*" is: he refrained and avoided. It is said: "*'afat al-ibil al-ma'*" (the camels refused the water) when they do not drink. The same is said of other than camels.

And the *zajir* is also like the *'a'if*. It is said: he drives the birds with *zajr*. That is because he looks at birds and decides about them like the *'a'if*. If he sees something he dislikes, he turns back from a matter he wants to begin or a need he wants to fulfill. The *zajir* means the forbidder, as if the bird had driven him away from that action, or that whoever took an omen from it drove him away from that. The meaning of *zajr* may also be that when he sees something of them, he shouts at them and drives them away, so his driving them away is a *zajr* for them. From this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Leave the birds in their nests."

I say: when they did not see a *sanih* or a *barih*, they would startle the birds to see in which direction they flew. And God knows best.

Abu Hatim said: The origin of this is that they used to drive away birds, then they drove away gazelles and foxes, and used the human voice, deriving from its utterance and other things. Then all of these were attributed to birds, so it was said: "*yatatayyar*," that is, he derives omens from birds.

It is narrated from al-Asma'i who said: I asked Ibn 'Awn: "What is *al-fa'l*?" He said: It is that you are sick and hear: "O Salim!" and you are seeking something and hear: "O finder!"

He said: Ibn Sirin disliked *tiyara* and loved *fa'l*. In a hadith: "The most truthful of omens is *fa'l*." *Al-fa'l* is derived from *al-fiyal*, which is a game they gamble with. They would take dirhams and mix them with dust, then pile them up for a long time, then divide them into two halves, and draw lots over them. Whoever was struck by the lot chose one of the two halves. Since the one who makes an omen of it (*mufa'il*) chose from them what he liked, it was called *fa'l*, because he takes an omen from what he loves. This was common among the Arabs, and most of it was among the Banu Asad.

Al-Asma'i said: Sa'd ibn Nasr told me that a group of jinn discussed the augury of the Banu Asad. They came to them and said: "Our she-camel has strayed, so if you would send with us someone who takes omens..." So they said to a young boy among them: "Go with them." One of them carried him behind him on his mount. Then they set off, and an eagle with one wing broken met them. The boy shuddered and wept. They said to him: "What is wrong with you?" He said: "It broke one wing, and raised another, and swore by God openly that you are not human, and you do not seek a she-camel milk." They used to call the one that comes from your right and takes to your left *sanih*, and the one that comes from your left and takes on your right *barih*, and the one that meets you *nati'h* and *kafih*, and the one that comes from behind you *qa'id*, and the one that presents itself from every direction *mutih*. Some of them took an omen of ill from the *barih* and an omen of good from the *sanih*, and some of them took an omen of good from the *barih* and an omen of ill from the *sanih*.

Zuhayr said:

*They passed on the right, and I said to her: "Answer me!"*
*Scattered dates, when will the meeting be?"*

Al-Kumayt said:

*Nor the *sanih* birds, nor the *barih* birds in the evening,*
*Did the one with an unbroken horn pass by, or the one with a broken horn?*

They took omens by the sound horn and the broken horn. The *a'dab* is the one with one horn.

As for the *qa'if*, he is the one who follows tracks and knows them, and knows a man's resemblance in his child.

It is narrated from 'Awsajah ibn Mu'aqqib the tracker, who said: "Our palm trees were being stolen, so we recognized their tracks. They rode donkeys, and we recognized them by the touch of their hands and the clusters."

It seems the tracker was named *qa'if* because he follows the trail. It is said: "*qafa al-athar*" and "*qaf al-athar*," that is, he followed it.

Al-Asma'i said, from Abu Tarafah al-Hudhali, who said: Two trackers saw the track of a camel, while they were returning from 'Arafah a day or two after the people. One of them said: "A she-camel." The other said: "A male camel." They followed it, and found it: it was a hermaphrodite.

It is said of a man who is clever and knowledgeable about affairs: he is an *'a'if* and a *qa'if*.

Some of the Arabs did not take omens, and did not fear omens, and boasted of abandoning them, considering their abandonment courage and boldness. One of their poets said:

*I went out, and I was not one who would go out*
*on Waqi or Hatim*

*So the unlucky days were like the lucky days,*
*and the lucky days were like the unlucky days.*

Another said:

*I am not one who fears when his saddle is firm,*
*saying: "Waqi and Hatim have overtaken me today."*

*But he proceeds on that, advancing,*
*when the stumbling *khathārim* turns him away from those fears.*

(p-220) *Al-Kh̲athārim* (one who divines by birds): the one who takes omens from birds' movements. It is also said to mean *'iyāfa* (augury by birds' flight). *Qiyāfa* (tracing or physiognomic inference) concerns tracks and lines, and it too is a kind of soothsaying (*kahāna*). It consists of drawing lines on the ground lengthwise, then drawing lines across them, then casting pebbles, barley, or pieces of wood. The diviner keeps drawing, erasing, and redrawing, and then pronounces a judgment based on the pattern. Of the same type is *'ilm al-katf* (scapulimancy), which consists of looking at a sheep's shoulder blade and then reporting things that will happen in the world, such as wars, rain, winds, drought, fertility, and other matters. The one who does this is called a *kattāf*, as though the name were derived from *katf* (shoulder), just as *'arrāf* (diviner) is so named, because the *'arrāf* belongs to the category of *'iyāfa*. *'Iyāfa* and *'arāfa* are the same. All of these things, namely sorcery (*sihr*), soothsaying, *qiyāfa*, *'iyāfa*, drawing lines, tracing patterns, scapulimancy, and whatever resembles them, have been addressed in reports and narrations, and the discussion of them would be lengthy. All of them are abhorrent and forbidden. Some of them have received strict prohibition, such as sorcery and soothsaying, while for some of the lesser ones there is concession and leniency, such as *qiyāfa*, *'iyāfa*, and scapulimancy. End of quotation.

He (al-Biqā'ī) accepts this for *qiyāfa*, but disputes it for the others. Then he said: Most of these practices originated with the prophets (peace be upon them). When they are practised after abrogation (*naskh*) and after the Prophet ﷺ has forbidden them, they become forbidden and lead to unbelief, to *ta'ṭīl* (denial of God's attributes), and to other kinds of corruption. Then he said: As for what pertained to the polytheist Arabs, it has vanished so completely that it is not known, and there is no need to mention its manner, since it has disappeared and left no trace. (p-221) Nevertheless, jurists and scholars cannot dispense with knowing it, since it is mentioned in the Qur'an, and since it is obligatory for scholars to learn what is in the Qur'an according to their capacity. Ignorance of it is a deficiency on their part. And God knows best what is correct.

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 37, verse 29:

When He (glorified is He) indicated by naming this speech of theirs a question, showing that their intent was: "Will you then avail us anything, or bear for us a portion of the punishment?" — and it was as if it were said: "How did the leaders answer after this statement from the followers?" It is said: ﴿They will say, "Rather, you were not believers"﴾; that is, their disbelief was not the cause; rather, ﴿you were not believers﴾; that is, you were deeply rooted in this attribute by your innate natures. Therefore you followed us in what we commanded you, because it was in your character. This is evidence that whoever was not firmly established in faith was among them;

Then they reinforced this meaning with their words, negating what those on the right had alluded to: ﴿And there was not⦅for us⦆ over you⦅any⦆ authority﴾; that is, a settled state. They went to the extreme in negation with their words ﴿any authority﴾; that is, "we compelled you with that authority"; rather, you followed us by your own choice. This is the meaning of ﴿Rather, you were﴾; that is, by natural disposition and inherent nature, ﴿a people﴾; that is, possessing strength and sufficiency for what you attempt of affairs; ﴿transgressing﴾; that is, exceeding your measures, going to extremes in disbelief, and being excessive in sins and wrongdoing. And for this reason, you have a creation (p-222) in which you do not need great movement;

﴿فَحَقَّ عَلَيْنا﴾: that is, all of us, both we and you, came under this (judgment) because of that. They expressed it in a way that shows their regret, so they said: ﴿قَوْلُ رَبِّنا﴾, that is, of our Lord, whose kindness toward us we met with disbelief, and whose nurturing of us we repaid with ingratitude. His word is the judgment of misguidance, because of what was in our hearts of readiness for it and refusal of faith, so the judgment is punishment.

When they grasped the gross error they had fallen into, away from the clear path, and knew that no one abandons such a path except under the compulsion of a compeller, they concluded that only the rights of the Supreme Word had forced them into it. They knew that just as they had come under its judgment in disbelief, they would come under its judgment in punishment. So, overcome by the anguish that had seized them, and intending by the emphasis to cut off the followers' hopes (from what their words had implied, that the leaders could avail them anything), they said: ﴿إنّا﴾, that is, all of us together, ﴿لَذائِقُونَ﴾, that is, we are indeed going to taste the terrible punishment with which the threat was made against us.

When they had exhausted the residue of their regret, lamentation and complaint, they returned to completing that speech, and said: ﴿So we misled you﴾; that is, we led you astray and caused you to fall into error, by reason of the obligations of that statement upon us. Then they gave the reason for that, saying - emphasizing also, in refutation of what the followers had claimed, that the leaders were not the cause of their being led astray except the chiefs: ﴿Indeed we﴾; that is, all of us together; ﴿were erring﴾; that is, in our very nature was straying (al-ghiwayah), which is deviating from the straight path to ruinous destinations.

(p-223) When the leaders said to them what the truth of their matter was, which necessitated the judgment of their partnership, he (exalted) made as its consequence His saying, emphasizing it to repel the one who imagines that the punishment is restricted to the cause: ﴿Indeed, they﴾, i.e., the two groups, ﴿because of what they said about themselves﴾, ﴿on that Day﴾, i.e., the day on which this mutual speech took place among them, ﴿will be partners in the punishment﴾, i.e., the greatest punishment, ﴿in its essence﴾. Yet they differ in its description according to the degrees of their disbelief, just as they were partners in the cause while differing in the intensity of their share in it and in their leniency.

Al-Bukhari said in his Sahih (authentic collection), in the tafsir (exegesis) of "Ha Mim al-Sajda": Al-Minhal related from Sa'id: A man said to Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both): "I find in the Qur'an things that seem contradictory to me." He said: ﴿So there will be no kinship between them that Day, nor will they ask one another﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 101]; ﴿And they will turn to one another, questioning each other﴾ [al-Saffat: 27]; ﴿And they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾ [al-Nisa': 42]; ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 23]. So they concealed in this verse. And He said: ﴿The heaven — He constructed it﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 27], up to His saying: ﴿And after that He spread out the earth﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 30]; so He mentioned the creation of the heaven before the creation of the earth. Then He said: ﴿Do you indeed disbelieve in the One who created the earth in two days?﴾ [Fussilat: 9], up to: ﴿obedient﴾ [Fussilat: 11]; so He mentioned in this verse the creation of the earth before the heaven. And He said: "And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful"; "Mighty and Wise"; "Hearing and Seeing." It was as if He had been, then He passed on and said: ﴿So there will be no kinship between them﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 101], at the first blast. Then the Trumpet will be blown, (p-224) and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth will fall unconscious, except whom Allah wills. So there will be no kinship at that time, nor will they ask one another. Then at the final blast they will turn to one another, questioning each other. As for His saying: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 23] and ﴿And they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾ [al-Nisa': 42]: Allah forgives the sins of the people of sincerity, while the polytheists said, "Come, let us say: we were not polytheists," so their mouths were sealed and their hands spoke. At that point it became known that Allah does not have any statement concealed from Him. And ﴿At that time those who disbelieved will wish﴾ [al-Nisa': 42], the verse. And He created the earth in two days, then He created the heaven, then ﴿He turned to the heaven and made them complete seven heavens﴾ [al-Baqarah: 29] in two other days, then He spread out the earth. And "spread out" ﴿[dahaha]﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 30] means He brought forth from it water and pasture, and created the mountains, the hills, and what is between them in two other days. That is His saying: ﴿He spread it out﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 30], and His saying: ﴿He created the earth in two days﴾ [Fussilat: 9]. So the earth and what is in it were made in four days, and the heavens were created in two days. "And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful": He named Himself thus, and that is His saying, meaning He has always been so. Indeed Allah does not will a thing except that He achieves what He wills. So let the Qur'an not appear contradictory to you, for all of it is from Allah.

And in the surah of "al-Mursalat" he said: Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) was asked about: ﴿This is a Day on which they will not speak﴾ [al-Mursalat: 35], ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 23], and ﴿Today We will seal their mouths﴾ [Ya-Sin: 65]. He said: It has various states: at one time they speak, and at another time He seals upon them.

(p-225) When He, glory be to Him, had informed of their being partners (in the punishment), He began a fresh statement to magnify the matter of their punishment, and to point to its generality in both abodes for everyone who shared with them in criminality. So He said, emphasizing (it), to repel the assumption of one who denies the Resurrection, and the assumption of one who sees the respite granted to the criminal in this world as a blessing and denies that it is a retribution, or who, in persisting in criminality, acts like one who denies (it): ﴿Indeed We﴾, that is, by the majesty We possess, which nothing escapes; ﴿thus﴾, that is, the like of this act, which is of great importance; ﴿do﴾ with them. This was originally the (grammatical) structure, but He attached it to the attribute, for generalization and for giving the reason, so He said: ﴿with the criminals﴾, that is, everyone who severs what Allah has commanded to be joined, in this world and in the Hereafter. We grant respite, then We seize them with a severe seizure, by which those who were partners in wrongdoing become enemies who dispute with one another and shift blame onto one another; then that will not benefit them, rather We make them share in the punishment.

Then he gave the reason for their punishment in His words, emphasizing the wonder at them, because their act is deserving of being denied, since no sensible person would believe that anyone could be arrogant toward this statement, for there is nothing more just than it: ﴿Indeed, they were﴾; that is, always, ﴿when it was said to them﴾; that is, by whatever speaker it was said: ﴿There is no god﴾; that is, possible; and when the possible is negated, the existent is more fitting, for nothing exists except what is possible for it to exist, even if it is necessary; ﴿except Allah﴾; that is, the Sovereign Most High, distinct from all existents in His essence, attributes, and acts, as is the truth, ﴿so that they would single Him out for divinity, just as He is singular in creating﴾, as is not hidden from anyone who has the least grasp of the attributes of perfection. He placed the negation first because adornment (tahliyah) is only after clearing away (takhliyah). ﴿They used to be arrogant﴾; that is, they produced arrogance by refusing to affirm this truth, than which nothing is more just, and by refusing to follow the one who calls to it, the arrogance of one who seeks greatness for himself and from others, because of the obstinacy and rebelliousness in it. So there was no barrier for them from the seven gates of Hell, each word of this statement together with its accompanying witness to its sending being a barrier from one of those gates; otherwise, in some of the hours of their days, which by the number of their letters are twenty-four, there would have been some good that would save them from hardships.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 37, verse 36:

When he had informed that they were arrogant toward the Tawhid (oneness) of God, he followed it with the information that they spoke about His Messenger (ﷺ) in a way He does not approve. So He said: ﴿And they would say﴾; that is, at all times; by which they showed how far they were from faith, in the utmost distance, by putting their saying in the form of a denying interrogative, emphasized: ﴿Shall we really leave our gods﴾; that is, worshipping them. The emphasis of the original statement was for indicating that their denial proceeds from them while they know that every scholar of their condition sees them as deserving to abandon what they are upon, because of what he (ﷺ) brought. Therefore He informed that what they are upon is obstinacy, by putting their denial in a manner of known contradiction by self-evidence, with His saying: ﴿for a mad poet?﴾; for madness has no order with it, while poetry requires a sound intellect, a upright purpose, and a sound natural disposition for meter. Or it is for indicating that denying the emphasized is denying what is other than it by way of a fortiori argument.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 37, verse 37:

Since their intention by this was that his speech is false, for most of a poet's speech is exaggeration and falsehood, and the speech of a madman is confused, it was as if He said in reply to them: he did not come with poetry, nor with madness; ﴿Rather, he came with the truth﴾; that is, the perfect one in truthfulness.

Since what he brought was worthy of being true and of being accepted, even if it opposed all the people of the earth; and it was, along with that, in agreement with those whose truthfulness had been established and whose following by people was well known; so he was worthy that these people should accept it, those who had lowered themselves from the peak of knowing men by the truth to the depths of knowing the truth by their claimed knowledge of men; so the outcome of their affair became imitation (taqlid). He said: ﴿And he confirmed the messengers﴾; that is, those whom every person of understanding knows to be the most complete full moons by whom Allah lit up the universes at every time; and it preceded at the end of Surah "Fatir" that they (the disbelievers) blamed whoever denied them, and swore by Allah with their most emphatic oaths that if a warner came to them, they would surely be guided by him; then they denied; by denying their master with this contradictory speech.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 37, verse 38:

When they reached this degree of tyranny, manifest falsehood, and calumny, the listener yearned to learn their recompense, so He resumed the report of it, presenting it in the mode of direct address to indicate that wrath had reached its limit. He said, in the form of emphasis, negating what they hoped for, namely intercession by those whom they claimed would bring them near to God in nearness (p-228), and as an admonition to them and to their like in this world, regarding what they deny, whether literally or figuratively: ﴿Indeed you﴾; that is, O you addressed in contempt; the criminals; ﴿are certainly to taste﴾; that is, for what you used to constrict upon the friends of God; ﴿the painful punishment﴾.

Since He, glorified is He, is the Judge, the Just, who does not wrong anyone even to the weight of an atom, He does not add anything to their recompense beyond what they deserve, although He is free to do whatever He wills, and His action, however it occurs, is only justice. So He said: ﴿And you are not recompensed﴾; that is, while the state is that you are not, ﴿except what﴾; that is, the like of what [you did]. Since they were disposed to those evil characteristics, He made clear that these were a nature for them, from which they could not free themselves, by expressing it with the particle of being (kāna): so He said: ﴿You used to do﴾ (kuntum taʿmalūn), negating the illusion of one who might suppose that they did something without His decree, glorified is He.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 37, verse 40:

Since among those addressed by this there are those whom God knows will believe, and [God] made an exception from the waw of "tasters" (dhā'iqū), He said—encouraging them to faith, and indicating that what keeps them steadfast in the misguidance they are upon is nothing but the deceit of hearts through showing off and other things; so it is an exception connected (ittiṣāl) in light of this subtle consideration—: ﴿Except the servants of God﴾. So He encouraged them through the attribute of servanthood, than which nothing is more honorable, and He attributed them—for added appeal—to the Greatest Name (al-ism al-a'ẓam) (p-229), which indicates all the attributes of perfection; and He increased their desire through the attribute than which no attribute is more exalted, so He said: ﴿the sincere ones (al-mukhlaṣīn)﴾

When He had delivered them from among them, He mentioned what is theirs, and He said, exalting them with the particle of distance: ﴿Those﴾; that is, those of lofty rank, for they purified their souls from the turbidity of desires; ﴿for them is a known provision﴾; that is, they know its absent and its present, its arrival, its taste, its benefit, its measure, its outcome, and all that it is possible to know of its affairs; and they are not like what they are in in this abode of troubling dangers: ﴿and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow﴾ [Luqman: 34]; because the soul is more at rest with what is known, and more able to be at ease with it.

Since the people of Paradise do not eat for sustenance and need, but for enjoyment, delight and gladness; because their bodies are perfected and created for eternity, they have no need to preserve their health. So He said: ﴿Fruits﴾; that is, they enjoy them, with what they had strained of their life in this world. And since that which is the bodily pleasure is not praised with the utmost praise except together with honor, which is the nourishment of the spirit, He said: ﴿And they will be honored﴾; He built it in the passive form to indicate that the existence of their being honored by everything is a certainty that cannot be otherwise at all.
Since honor (al-ikram) is not complete except together with a pleasant abode, He said: ﴿In gardens of bliss﴾; that is, those in which nothing other than it can be imagined.

Since enjoyment is not complete except with loved companions, and since it is the custom of kings to be exclusive in the highest place, he made clear that they are all kings. So He said: ﴿On couches, facing one another.﴾ That is: none of them has his face turned away from the face of the other, despite the large number.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 37, verse 45:

Since that (the delight described) cannot be complete without drink, and since the intended point is the circulating of it (the drink) and not that it comes from a specific source, He said: ﴿Yutaf⁠〹〹〹 (it is circulated)﴾; with the verb in the passive form (lil-maf'ul, passive voice). And it is as if it (the cup) is lowered down to them from above, so that it is more noble for it and better protected; so He alerted to that with the particle of elevation (al-isti'la', "upon"), and said: ﴿ʿalayhim﴾ (upon them), that is, while they are above their couches like kings; ﴿bi-ka's﴾ (with a cup), that is, a vessel containing wine. They said: even if there is no wine in the glass, it is still a qadah (goblet); and it is not called ka's (cup) unless wine is in it; ﴿min maʿin﴾ (from a flowing spring), that is, from wine flowing in its rivers, apparent to the eyes, gushing as water gushes; they do not have to treat it with pressing, nor does anything compel them to be gentle with it, nor is there any shortfall in it of any kind.
