This is because it is the nature of that which descends upon a thing without the permission of its owner, and it does not overcome a place except that it has already overcome its people. So it kneels upon them with a kneeling such that they cannot, while it is there, come out into that courtyard, which is the open space free of dwellings. It is as if it were the speaker of the people, and the place of their rest, whatever the time, whether night or day, is where it kneels. But since their custom was to raid at dawn, He said, by way of illustration, indicating with the fa' (so) that this is the cause and not anything else: ﴿evil is the morning of those who were warned﴾, that is: those among these and others who are fit to be frightened. This threat cannot apply except to the Day of the Conquest, and whoever was not prepared for anything other than warning was in the utmost evil on that day. These are the ones whom the Prophet (ﷺ) killed on that day; among them were some who clung to the curtains of the Ka'bah, but that did not benefit them. However, they were few. As for the rest, if that morning was grievous to behold for them, then by the life of Allah, its news gladdened them.

(p-317) Since the Prophet ﷺ was a prophet of mercy, who would not uproot his people with punishment, he said, indicating this by repeating the command, as an emphasis for consolation and a promise of victory, and with what it contains of additional meaning beyond the first, conjoining it to the first "tawalla" (turn away): ﴿And turn away﴾; that is: impose upon yourself patience with them on that day when the second punishment descends upon them, and turn away ﴿from them for a time﴾. And so the Prophet ﷺ did; for he descended upon their courtyard in the morning of the Day of the Conquest (Yawm al-Fath), and they were unable to resist.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 37, verse 179:

When some of them persisted in obstinacy and resistance, they were not slow to turn their backs and seek safety by entering into what he (ﷺ) had made a sign of security. Ḥamās ibn Qays, a brother of Banū Bakr, said, when he entered his house, to his wife: "Close the door on me." She reproached him for his flight, after she had been forbidding him from opposing the Muslims, and he would not desist, and he said to her: "I must make some of them serve you," and he recited:

Indeed, had you witnessed the Day of al-Ḥandama,
When Ṣafwān fled and ʿIkrima fled,
And the Muslim swords met us,

(Lines lacking here in the source text.)

Cutting off every forearm and skull,
Striking, so that nothing is heard but murmuring,
I forbade our people and their mutterings against them.
You did not utter, in blame, even a single word.

When this applied to the Day of Conquest, and that day had placed the unbelievers in a station where they had no standing, He said: ﴿And look﴾, omitting their pronoun, i.e., look at what you wish of your affairs, those which concern you to consider; as for them, they became such that no regard is paid to them, their matter is not contemplated, and they are not turned to. Indeed We replaced their might with humiliation, and their multitude with paucity, and We cleansed those lands of the filth of polytheism, and We settled in them the purity of glorification and the sanctity of praise. And so it was, for he (ﷺ) said to them while he stood on the steps of the Kaaba, with them beneath him like sheep gathered on a rainy day, after he had said: "There is no god but Allah alone, without partner; He fulfilled His promise, supported His servant, honoured His army, and defeated the confederates alone." Then he said: "What do you think I will do with you, O assembly of Quraysh?" They said: (p-319) "Good. A noble brother and the son of a noble brother." He said: "Go, for you are the freed ones (al-Ṭulaqāʾ)." Ṣafwān ibn Umayya said to him: "Give me a choice of two months." He said: "You have a choice of four months." He did not compel any of them to accept Islam, yet after that they all embraced Islam willingly, one after another. When he besieged al-Ṭāʾif and it proved difficult for him, he withdrew from it; then they soon sent their envoys to him and embraced Islam, and their Islam was good, and none of them apostatized in the apostasy (al-ridda). This is part of the meaning of ﴿So they will see﴾.

Since there was established for Him, glorified be He, of greatness what was mentioned, so that the command is His command and the creation is His creation, His transcendence above every deficiency and His being described with every perfection became established. Therefore the outcome of that was closing with the comprehensive forms of declaring Him free of imperfection and praising Him. So He said: ﴿Glory be to your Lord﴾; that is, the One who bestows favour upon you by sending you, and by establishing the manifest, clear proof of your truthfulness through whatever the states of your enemies may be, whether speech or silence; and by strengthening you with every power and clothing you with every awe; ﴿the Lord of might﴾; that is, the might which He alone possesses, as the idafa (construct phrase) conveys; and it conveys what the witness of existence and the judgement of reason attest. It has been known from what was mentioned in this surah that might overcomes everything and nothing overcomes it. In the idafa of the Lord to Him and to might there is an indication of His exclusive possession of might, on behalf of the Prophet (ﷺ) and of everyone who agrees with him in his affair, over all creation, even if the outward appearance seems otherwise; ﴿above what they describe﴾; that is, what entails deficiencies, because of what has been established (p-320) of their misguidance and their remoteness from the truth.

Since He had already singled out, in this surah, those of His messengers upon whom He wished peace, He generalized it to them all, saying, coordinating with "Glory be to" (subhan): ﴿And peace﴾; that is, glorification of Him, safety, honor, pride, and exaltedness; ﴿upon the messengers﴾; that is, those who describe Him with what is fitting for Him, whom He chose; the ones who stand in rows (al-Saffat, "those who set the ranks in rows"); the ones who drive away with a driving (al-Zajirat, "those who drive away"); the ones who recite a reminder (al-Talinat, "those who recite the reminder"); from among mankind and the angels, those mentioned in this surah and others; because of what He, glorified is He, decreed for them from eternity of might and victory.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 37, verse 182:

﴿And praise﴾; that is, the encompassing of the attributes of perfection; ﴿belongs to Allah﴾; that is, the One who gathers all the Most Beautiful Names (al-Asma' al-Husna, the divine names of perfection), which the totality of His creation points to. He alluded to this with His saying: ﴿Lord of the worlds﴾. Thus He is then the One, the Exalted (al-Mu'tal), who is far beyond having equals, likenesses, peers, or counterparts, in everything, in sayings, actions, affairs, and states. The end of this, as you see, has joined with its beginning, and its joints and connections have embraced one another. And Allah is the Guide to what is right.
